title: Rejectors in the Wild: Deployment Barriers for LLM Rejectors

problem.claim: LLM hallucinations hinder reliable deployment in high-risk domains, motivating systems that abstain when answers are likely incorrect.

gap.claim: Separated rejectors for black-box LLMs have important limitations related to correctness definitions, cross-model redundancies, and abstention-based execution.

contributions.claim: A human-annotation study examines how different definitions of correctness affect which rejector appears reliable.
A large-scale 95×95 cross-model transfer analysis identifies structured redundancies between rejectors across LLMs.
Two pruning strategies construct a compact, diversity-preserving LLM pool, and a router selects the most reliable model per query as part of a shift from abstention to selective execution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed router is reported to outperform common routing baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hallucinations limit reliable LLM deployment in high-risk domains.
Selective prediction and separated rejectors can abstain from likely incorrect queries in black-box or cost-constrained settings.
The paper studies correctness definitions and structured redundancies between rejectors, and reframes the task from abstention toward selective execution.
Pruning strategies create a compact LLM pool and a router selects the most reliable model per query.

source_observation.claim: The apparent reliability of a rejector can change substantially with the definition of correctness.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation criteria are part of the deployment design and can alter comparative conclusions.

application.claim: Specify and test correctness definitions before selecting or deploying a rejector.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which correctness definitions are appropriate for particular applications.

source_observation.claim: Rejectors across LLMs exhibit structured redundancies that can support pruning and routing.

interpretation.claim: Model diversity may enable compact pools without relying on every available model.

application.claim: Use cross-model analysis to design diversity-preserving model pools and query-level routers.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the tasks, costs, or conditions under which the reported routing advantage holds.

unknowns: Datasets, task domains, and evaluation protocols are unspecified.
Quantitative results and baseline details are unspecified.
The operational definition of selective execution is unspecified.
